root.name: Pirc Defense: 150 Attack
root.moves: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nf6 3. Nc3 g6 4. Be3 c6 5. Qd2

overview: White plays Be3 and Qd2 with Bh6, h3 and often g4 or h4-h5 to attack the fianchettoed king, while Black answers with ...b5, ...Nbd7 and a queenside or central counter (...e5, ...Qa5). Most games show either 5.h3 (the Sveshnikov-Jansa set-up) or 5...Bg4. It is imbalanced and tactical, but Black's structure is sound.

white_ideas.idea: Qd2 and Bh6 to trade Black's fianchettoed bishop
h3, g4 and h4-h5 pawn storm on the kingside
Castle long and keep the big e4-d4 centre

black_ideas.idea: ...Bg4 (Inner Doll) to pin and trade a defender

typical_structures.structure: e4-d4 White centre against ...c6/...d6 with a fianchettoed Bg7

character.notes: Reputation for opposite-side castling and fast kingside attacks; Black needs counterplay in time.

gambit.notes: No material is given up on purpose.

soundness.notes: Sound for Black; White's attack is dangerous but not refuting.

structure.notes: White keeps e4-d4 while Black prepares ...e5 or ...b5; centre undecided.

approach.notes: Mainstream branch of the Pirc against Be3, played by strong players.

level.notes: Plans and timing matter more than memorised lines.

plan_phrases: Bh6 to trade the fianchetto bishop

sublines_that_differ.name: Inner Doll Defense
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 d6 2. d4 Nf6 3. Nc3 g6 4. Be3 c6 5. Qd2 Bg4
sublines_that_differ.how: Black pins early and trades a defender rather than starting with ...b5.

character.reason: Opposite-side castling and a Bh6/h4-h5 attack make both sides race.

soundness.reason: Black's set-up is respectable and used at elite level.

structure.reason: The big centre is neither locked nor traded; Black chooses between ...e5 and ...b5 breaks.

approach.reason: A main anti-Pirc set-up that strong players choose.

level.reason: Plans and timing of the pawn storms and counters matter more than long forced lines.

plans.reason: White aims at the kingside with Bh6 and pawn storms while Black hits the large centre.
